description: Indulge in the rich, creamy goodness of Classic Butter Chicken, a beloved Indian culinary masterpiece. This Murgh Makhani recipe features tender chicken pieces simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, enriched with butter, cream, and aromatic spices. It is a harmonious blend of sweet and savory flavors, perfect for a comforting and satisfying meal.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken cubes with plain yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 tsp garam masala, lemon juice, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter or oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Sear the chicken for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onions and saute until they turn soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another 2 minutes until aromatic.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and salt. Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates from the gravy, about 10-12 minutes. This is crucial for a rich flavor. Add the soaked cashews and 1/2 cup water, then bring to a simmer.

instructions.title: Blend and Refine the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth. If using a regular blender, pass the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture. Return the pan to low heat.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the smooth gravy. Stir in the remaining 1 tsp garam masala, crushed Kasuri Methi, and sugar. Mix well and let it simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the gravy. Finally, stir in the fresh cream. Heat through for 1-2 minutes without boiling. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.

tips: For a richer flavor, marinate the chicken overnight in the refrigerator. This allows the spices to penetrate deeper into the meat.
Always use good quality, ripe tomatoes for the puree to get the best color and natural sweetness in your gravy. If fresh tomatoes are unavailable, canned crushed tomatoes can be a good substitute.

Adjust the amount of chili powder and green chilies according to your spice preference. A pinch of Kashmiri chili powder adds vibrant red color without adding too much heat, which is traditional for Butter Chicken.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in its native India as Murgh Makhani, is more than just a dish; it's a culinary icon. This beloved Indian chicken recipe has captivated palates worldwide with its rich, creamy, and subtly sweet yet tangy tomato-based gravy. Originating from the bustling streets of Delhi, it represents the epitome of comfort food, offering a luxurious experience that balances complex spices with the smooth, comforting embrace of butter and cream. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore the vibrant world of Indian cuisine, mastering authentic Butter Chicken is a rewarding journey that promises delectable results.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s, where enterprising chefs combined leftover tandoori chicken with a rich tomato gravy. The genius lay in the fusion of smoky, marinated chicken with a luscious sauce made from pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a generous amount of butter and cream. The distinctive flavor profile comes from a careful balance of spices like garam masala, fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), and often a touch of sugar to cut through the acidity of the tomatoes. The result is a vibrant orange-red gravy that is incredibly smooth, aromatic, and undeniably indulgent, making it one of the most popular Indian chicken recipes globally.

## Ingredients You Need for Authentic Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Murgh Makhani requires a thoughtful selection of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices. Here's what you'll need:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili for color, regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for finishing
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 fresh large tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, optional, but recommended for creaminess)
*   1-2 green chilies, slit (optional, for heat)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri)
*   1 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1/2 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Butter Chicken

Follow these steps to create an unforgettable Butter Chicken:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken**: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for best flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken**: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Set aside. For an authentic smoky flavor, you can grill or broil the chicken until slightly charred.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base**: In the same skillet or a deep pot, melt 2 tablespoons butter with 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent and softened, about 5-7 minutes.
4.  **Aromatics and Spices**: Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and turmeric powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to bloom the spices.
5.  **Tomatoes and Cashews**: Pour in the crushed tomatoes (or pureed fresh tomatoes). If using soaked cashews, drain them and add them to the pot. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down.
6.  **Blend the Gravy**: Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until absolutely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot.
7.  **Finish the Gravy**: Return the smooth gravy to the pot over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces. Stir in the garam masala, crushed kasoori methi, sugar, and salt to taste. Simmer for 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the gravy's flavors.
8.  **The Final Touch**: Stir in the heavy cream and a knob of butter (about 1-2 tablespoons). Heat gently for a few minutes until warmed through, but do not boil after adding cream, as it can curdle.
9.  **Garnish and Serve**: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Your authentic Murgh Makhani is ready to be enjoyed!

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key**: The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination is highly recommended.
*   **Smoky Chicken Flavor**: If you have a grill or broiler, charring the marinated chicken slightly before adding it to the gravy will impart an authentic tandoori flavor that elevates the dish significantly.
*   **Smooth Gravy is Essential**: Don't skip blending the gravy thoroughly. For an ultra-smooth consistency, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending. This removes any fibrous bits from onions or tomatoes.
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder**: This spice is crucial for achieving the signature vibrant red-orange color of Murgh Makhani without adding excessive heat.
*   **Kasoori Methi**: Dried fenugreek leaves are a non-negotiable ingredient. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their distinctive, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is characteristic of Butter Chicken.
*   **Balance the Flavors**: The sugar in the recipe is important to balance the acidity of the tomatoes. Adjust it to your preference. A little extra butter at the end also enhances richness and sheen.
*   **Resting Time**: Like many stews and curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments. For a truly authentic Indian dining experience, serve your Murgh Makhani with:

*   **Naan Bread**: Soft, fluffy naan is perfect for soaking up every drop of the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan adds an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Basmati Rice**: Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a light contrast to the rich curry.
*   **Roti or Paratha**: Whole wheat flatbreads like roti or flaky paratha are also excellent choices.
*   **Cooling Sides**: A simple cucumber raita (yogurt dip) or a fresh green salad can provide a refreshing counterpoint to the creamy curry.
*   **Pickles and Chutneys**: A side of mango pickle or mint chutney can add an extra zing.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is a masterpiece, it's also adaptable to different preferences and dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani**: For a delicious meat-free version, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cheese) to make Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu for a vegan-friendly option. Simply pan-fry the paneer or tofu until golden before adding it to the finished gravy.
*   **Vegan Butter Chicken**: Replace butter with a plant-based butter alternative or coconut oil. For the cream, use full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream for a rich, dairy-free gravy. Ensure your yogurt for marination is also plant-based.
*   **Nut-Free Option**: If you have a cashew allergy, you can omit them entirely or substitute with 1-2 tablespoons of sunflower seeds (soaked) or a tablespoon of cornstarch slurry mixed in at the end to thicken the gravy.
*   **Spice Level**: Adjust the amount of green chilies and red chili powder to suit your preferred level of heat. For a milder curry, omit green chilies and use only Kashmiri chili powder.
*   **Tomato Type**: While canned crushed tomatoes offer convenience and consistent flavor, fresh, ripe plum tomatoes, pureed and strained, can also be used for a brighter, fresher taste.

Butter Chicken is a testament to the magic of Indian cuisine – a dish that’s both comforting and exotic, familiar yet exciting. By following this guide, you can recreate the authentic flavors of Murgh Makhani in your own kitchen and savor a truly classic Indian chicken recipe. Enjoy the journey of bringing this culinary masterpiece to your table!
